findings.surface: TLS ALPN / HTTP/2 on the production data listener
findings.claim: The one production HTTPS data listener offers only http/1.1 in ALPN and configures only hyper's HTTP/1 builder, so a client offering only h2 gets TLS alert 120 no_application_protocol. Recorded AWS endpoints negotiate h2; every HTTP/2-only streaming data plane (bedrock-runtime ConverseStream, kinesis SubscribeToShard, hand-signed HTTP/2 Kinesis PutRecord/GetRecords) is unreachable. 16 open docs (4 wire, 10 behavioral, 2 unclassified) and 3 open GitHub issues describe this class; two fixed docs claiming an ALPN fix are reopened by later reports. The separate resource http() listener does offer h2, but it does not serve the data port.
findings.root_cause: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/server/src/lib.rs:1379-1399 defines DATA_LISTENER_ALPN = &[b"http/1.1"] and data_listener_tls_config() stamps that onto rustls ServerConfig::alpn_protocols; :1252-1254 and :1323-1328 use it in serve_production_on_address and call http_builder().http1() only. /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/server/src/listeners.rs:34-35, :386-388 offers [h2, http/1.1] only for Listeners::http() resource listeners. /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/server/src/tls_certificate_authority.rs:90-98 builds the base config with no ALPN. This is one process-wide transport choice, not per-service code.

findings.surface: error Code/Message/envelope shapes across all protocol families
findings.claim: Every framework-level refusal is rendered from a fixed two-member envelope: JSON {__type, lowercase message}, Query XML <Error><Type>Sender</Type><Code/><Message/></Error>, restXml <ErrorResponse>, or CBOR {__type, message}. Service::override_refusal can replace only a code and a sentence; it cannot populate modeled error members (Message, RequestId, requestId, reason, code, resourceId, resourceType, invalidParameter) or add headers. 497 of 1229 wire docs carry an error-code/message divergence key (1742 keys: 618 lowercase $.message, 239 $.Message, 273 x-amzn-errortype, 195 __type, 417 Query/EC2 error-body keys); 243 of 436 service.rs leave override_refusal at its default None.

gaps: No emulator was built or run, no simparity replay, no curl and no live AWS request. Every AWS-side statement is recorded behavior from the in-repo traces, issue docs or GitHub reporters; code facts are static reads of HEAD ec5f6fbab9238221b966379f06846c34e9d6a6f5.

Open docs are not a HEAD-state census: docs are filed against older Issue-Commit SHAs and carry an explicit drift note; some are marked fixed in the 17671-row fixed-doc index while still open elsewhere, and some fixed docs are reopened by later reports. C-19 lists the concrete conflicts. The repository history available here is one squashed commit, so per-file fix dates could not be recovered.

No authoritative AWS-side list of services that support rpcv2Cbor was available. The 25-of-436 model census is a local fact; the claim that more services should declare it rests only on GH #284 and the tagging API fixed doc and is marked unverified.

Protocol-family counts are exhaustive regex matches over doc titles, descriptions, evidence, steps and Issue-Key values; families overlap and no doc was assigned to exactly one family. The exact counts from parsing all 8971 wire Issue-Key lines are in the coverage string.

Generated OUT_DIR service declarations (service_decl.rs) are not on disk; the generated protocol table was inferred from the 440 model JSONs and the macro expansion in vendor/smithy-macros/src/lib.rs.
The 17671 fixed-doc rows were searched by title and filename only, not full text; a matching open doc may still have been fixed at HEAD without its fixed counterpart mentioning the same words.

The recorded AWS Content-Length: 0 on 204 responses conflicts with the HTTP/1.1 rule that forbids Content-Length on 204; whether hyper would let a handler-set header survive on the socket path was not tested.

The LinkedIn post's five checks (presigned S3 PUT content-type, unsigned SigV4, function URL auth, EventBridge/SQS policy, DynamoDB ACTIVE) are an external reporter's claims, not AWS ground truth, and were not used as evidence.

7114 stub rows and the thousands of per-operation handlers were not audited individually; this lens deliberately concentrated on the shared framework under vendor/server, vendor/smithy-server-runtime, vendor/smithy-schema-server, vendor/smithy-macros and services/common.

SigV4 chunk-signature chaining, trailer checksum validation and CORS header propagation were read statically only; their runtime behavior (especially in embedded mode versus socket mode) is unverified.
No parity claim is made: the wire corpus (1229 open docs), behavioral corpus (3605 open docs), 572 GitHub issues and 7114 stub rows remain open evidence of divergence.
